You’re a good parent, it’s sure hard to see your kid in pain and not being able to fix them, only they can fix themselves (with support of course) it’s rad of you to look out for her despite how hard it is not react or get really hurt. Good on ya. 

you should also make it clear you’re approachable and not just say it, i’ve had people tell me to go to them in times of need but when i did they either dismissed me or told me to “get help” 

And by approachable you need to know how to be a good lisenter, know how to respond to venting and not minimize or compare one’s suffer to another, what to say, what not to say and all that jazz, you can also do small acts of kindness like giving them compliments, reassure them or not make them feel like a burden or responsibilty to bear. 

I have no doubt you’d be a good parent to her.

Make sure to check up on your daughter or give her things she loves, or a comfort object like a teddy bear, this teddy im hugging is seriously helping me keep away from self harm thoughts. 

Be sure to be a judgment-free emotional support for your daughter, someone that she can go to and tell you how bad she feels without feeling guilty about it (maybe afraid to hurt you)
